She has a certain foreboding about one sister, which leads her to advise not letting her go begging. She looks forward to their meeting.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. For two days I have had no letters from you; I don't know why. Today I received one from the Superior saying you would write tomorrow, which would be today.

2. I am anxious to know how the conference went,1 and whether Assunta's son has died;2 I want to know how you found the Genoa house.

3. When you return you will have to bring Sr. A. Eletta, since Sr. A. Apanasia is no longer coming. My dear, what troubles! but patience; more in person.3

4. Listen, on your way back don't go to Nizza, because being with Eletta you cannot, and it is not fitting for us.4

5. I am worried about Sr. A. Santina, otherwise I would say you should bring the Superior to Piacenza for a while. Enough; for now leave Sr. A. Eletta in Genoa too, to keep the Superior company; we will move her another time. What do they say at the hospital?5

6. I want Sr. A. Santina not to go out

begging, but to send her sister and Sr. A. of the Saviour instead.6 For charity's sake, I don't know; there is a fear in me that I would remove if I could, so great is my fear. Let us hope it is only a bogey. Goodbye, because the priest is here and I want to post this. I am yours. Tomorrow I hope to receive letters from you. I am your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

7. If you go to the Countess, wait for a letter from me first,7 because I think that when you return from Genoa I shall be leaving here and we shall meet in Piacenza. From what I hear, they will soon let me go.8 Enough; I shall see from your letters what you tell me. It seems a hundred years since I saw you.

8. My Vincenza, try to do everything and see whether God might send a little providence. My God, my infamies permit this.

Give my warm greetings to the Superior and everyone; yours with all my heart, your affectionate MOTHER

She should not worry about not having accepted a girl. When there is no room, no other decision is possible. She should warn the Father to avoid meeting the Parish Priest: she has learned he is coming to inspect. These are terrible sufferings, but beautiful because they come to us from Jesus.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My Franceschina

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Yesterday I received two letters from you, one very long, the other about Parmigiani. You have done everything well; don't worry.1

2. My dear, since we have no room, what can we do?2 And when it is said politely, one can do no more.

3. I write to you in haste after dinner; or rather, this evening I will write to you together with that person.3

4. Meanwhile, for charity's sake, warn that person to arrange, if he can, not to see the Parish Priest and not to speak to him; for pity's sake, he is coming to scrutinize — I have just learned it; for charity's sake, let him notice nothing.4 Send him to S. Lazzaro, but in agreement with that person, so that he goes out and nothing is found there.5

5. My dear daughter, terrible but very beautiful [sorrows], because it is Jesus who sends them to us. I embrace them lovingly; I am glad to suffer, to grieve with our God! Patience and resignation be our two shields.6

Goodbye, goodbye; I am your affectionate

MOTHER ROSA

She has received a letter of commendation from Mgr Sciandra. Cardinal Vannicelli is continuing the revision of the Constitutions. The Archbishop of Bologna has visited the Ferrara community.

Your Most Reverend Excellency,

1. Knowing how welcome good news of the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne is to You, since it was born in Your bosom, I feel strictly bound to tell You at once the following.

2. These days I received the letter of commendation kindly given me by Mgr Sciandra, Bishop of Acqui, which praises the poor Daughters of Saint Anne beyond their deserts and declares his readiness to help them in every way he can.1

3. The Rule is being compiled entirely to my satisfaction. His Eminence Cardinal Vannicelli, the Saint God gave me as support in my many labours, is working with tireless zeal to complete everything.2

4. A week ago I had the good fortune to be visited by His Eminence Cardinal Morichini, Archbishop of Bologna; he blessed our house and the Community, and wished this poor Servant of the Lord the choicest blessings.

5. God grant that this most unworthy creature may profit by it by amending her wickedness.

6. Do not deprive me of Your Apostolic blessing, as I remain with veneration Your Most Reverend Excellency's

most humble Sr. A. MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

She warns her of some irregularities in the house and makes suggestions. She should remedy them prudently. May the Lord enlighten her and give her strength to do everything well.1

[My daughter],

1. In all confidence I warn you that your daughters grumble and that in their dormitory there is always chatter and no silence is kept. The dormitories are dirty, and so is the school.2

2. Listen, my daughter, I have arranged for the Superior in Genoa to send you the writing desks she had made for her schools, so they will serve very well for yours.3 Don Luigi will be pleased, because his little girls will be able to write better.4

3. I urge you to watch over what I wrote. If they need brooms, buy them, for charity's sake; I urge you not to let it be seen that I wrote to you, but with all prudence, little by little, find out where the trouble lies.5

2. Only now do I have the strength to stand, and first of all I address to Your Most Reverend Excellency the most fervent prayers of my soul, to obtain from Your kindly hand a word of approval signed on our Constitutions; this will free me from the most painful anguish, my mind being constantly agitated by fear about the approval. 3. Humbly at Your Feet, I implore Your fatherly Blessing, as with veneration I remain Your Most Reverend Excellency's

most humble Sr. A. MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

My daughter,

1. I hear from your letters of Sr. A. Teresa's poor health. Tell her in my name that the most beautiful miracle that we can be sure comes from God is that of obeying.1 When I hear that a daughter of Saint Anne, M. of the Immaculate, lies on a bed of pain, but wholly resigned, giving an example of obedience and truly practising this chief virtue heroically, then indeed one can say that, closing her eyes in the sleep of death, she flies straight into the arms of her God; but if it is otherwise, I do not know!!

2. St Rose of Lima, a great saint, knew, one might say, with seeing eyes, that what the doctor ordered made her worse, and yet out of obedience she took everything without a word; they bled her, she let herself be bled; they prescribed medicines, she took them all.

Giuseppa is doing night watches; I too had ordered that this Sister should never do night watches, given her poor health; so let another go, or let some other patient be left in order to care for this King's Prosecutor. She should cherish observance of the timetable, the Rule, meditation and silence, and impress on the sisters the value of obedience. For the examinations she should consult Mgr Mariano; for sea-bathing, the doctor. As for her wish to come to Piacenza, it does not seem prudent for her to leave a Community not yet well established. She is close to her in spirit, and one day they will be together for all eternity.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My blessed daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Here I am, all yours, today, the Holy Mother's day; I devote the whole hour of silence to my daughter.1 Alone in this little room, I want to put on paper a few things dictated by this perfect silence.

2. Listen, my dear, to what the heart of God, our all, says: "Whoever feeds on me will be sure of eternal life".2 So? Ah! if we could feed on Him at every moment, every second, what happiness it would be for us to have nothing to feed on but this Most Holy Bread! If we cannot have him bodily, let us try to receive him spiritually. Let us make a lively resolution in the morning, saying to dear Jesus: Today I want to receive you always, and I will keep my mind constantly occupied in making spiritual Communions. Little by little it becomes a habit. Even while talking let us invoke the sweet name of our beloved Jesus; with an act of love let us say to him: "Come, O my spouse, come, this heart wants you, it can no longer be without you. Come!".3

3. Daughter, to think that in the morning, when he comes down to us, he is a beautiful little child with tender limbs! He goes and sits, lies down inside our heart; and how carefully we must hold him so as not to hurt him, taking care that he does not have to suffer too much!4

4. There was a creature who, when she had him, felt him, and was so convinced that it was her Beloved walking about in that little room that all day she lived careful not to jostle and hurt him. She respectfully had regard for that part of herself and looked at it reverently, and delighting in the little child a loving word would escape her: "My dear Beloved, my joy" — what bliss she felt! She renewed Holy Communion spiritually, and then was filled with the keenest desire to love him, serve him, suffer for him and give her life for him alone.5

5. So? Would you like that? Try to do what these lines teach you, and you too will come to have what is written here.

6. Observance of the timetable in your community, the Rule, meditation and silence. Believe me, my dear, these are the points [on] which the whole edifice of good order rests. If these are kept exactly, you can be sure that all the rest are kept.6

7. In the conferences, make them feel the value of obedience: that we can have no good if we lack it, because whoever does not obey shows that she wants to do her own will, not God's, our only treasure. The Religious who does her own will is a shadow walking in the cloister without belonging to it.7

8. Now to what you ask: the examinations — do as you think. Listen, Mgr Mariano is coming on the 31st, and you can consult him and say that I wrote to you to that effect.8

9. I had said that if you had spoken to the doctor about bathing for your complaint — although I am very much against this treatment, since I don't much like a Religious going sea-bathing — nonetheless, since everyone does it nowadays, I submit to others' judgement; if he says no, so much the better.

10. As for your coming: I leave you free to come whenever you wish, but consider that you have no one to leave in your place. Resources are so scant, and besides, in a city where a hundred eyes are on you, who knows what might happen, your house being not yet firmly established and enclosed; and that sick woman, who may be in her grave at any moment; and surely these scatterbrains — who knows what they will do! What do you think? Are my observations fair? When this house is a little more firmly established and enclosed, when you no longer have Maria, and with good orders given, you can come whenever you like.9

11. This will certainly take some months, and meanwhile the longed-for news that makes me suffer so might come: I shall fly into your arms, because this will be the house where the Te Deum is sung.10

12. Be of good heart, for this mother of yours is always with you and every morning asks the Lord in particular to make you holy and give you the true spirit of the Holy Rule. Courage, be strong, for one day, if we have fought well, we shall wear the great decoration of honour on our breast and be together for an eternity. A great word, this, that weighs a whole world.11

13. When His Eminence comes, go and visit him and kiss his ring.12 Goodbye; the Lord bless you; believe me always your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

Greet everyone for me, imploring the choicest blessings on all. Greet Maria for me.13

Invitation to the girls' school display.1

Most Illustrious Sir,

1. On 1 August our poor little girls will give a simple display of their School Studies. I would be most fortunate if Your Lordship would honour me with your presence, and I dare hope so, recalling that you kindly attended in the past; you will thus be able to see their progress.

2. Confident that you will come, I venture to tell you that it will be at 5 in the afternoon.2

I take this opportunity to send you my warmest and most distinguished greetings, signing myself Your Lordship's most humble Sr. A. M. ROSA GATTORNO

If Sr. A. Panasia persists in her behaviour, she should send her straight to Piacenza. If she could finish the examinations and pay some debts, she might accompany her. Providence will come. They should pray to St Joseph to grant humility and, with this virtue, providence.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. I have just received yours and reply post-haste. I tell you that if Sr. A. Apanasia makes such scenes again, send her here to Piacenza at once, at once.1

2. If the Lord arranged things so that you could hold the examinations and pay the most urgent bills, then you could bring her here yourself, and so get a little rest.

3. For the rest, don't fret so much; we know that on this earth we have nothing but thorns. Providence will come; don't worry.2

4. I am sorry you have no patients; for charity's sake, let Sr. A. Giovanna never say such things again.3

5. God will think of us if we think of Him alone.4 Have the novena to St Joseph for providence repeated, and ask him to give you humility, and through this virtue to give you providence.

In haste, your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

God bless you all, and you in particular. The examinations at the Morte went splendidly; I hope yours will too.5

She did not reply at once for two reasons: her health and the boys' examinations... There are 148 and all did well. He asks about Ferrara. There is great poverty, but she has entrusted the work to God the Father's hands. She is glad to hear he may come to Piacenza; they can talk better in person about their troubles. All suffering vanishes when one considers the eternity of joy it earns.

A.M.F.

My good Father Agostino,

1. I have been slow to answer your most esteemed letter because I wanted to write in my own hand; first, my health, so desperate that I have nothing left — everything is consumed, only a wretched rag remains, which needs a prop every moment to stay on its feet; then I had the examinations of the boys at the Morte, who now number 148, all present, real jailbirds. If you had seen them: barefoot, one with his shirt hanging out of a hole in his trousers. They did splendidly, and the audience was satisfied; certainly they did not expect so much from such dreadful creatures.1

2. Now for two days I have had a little rest. You ask about Ferrara; that house, I can tell you, is in God the Father's hands, as I have laid everything to rest in him, and I will not worry about anything; the work is his, He will see to it. Poverty we have as much as we like; it covers our eyes.2

3. Have people pray a little, and pray yourself, that the good God may be moved to pity us, and then we shall have everything.3

4. Father Agostino, I see from your letter that by the end of this month you may be free and slip away here to Piacenza;4 this news gave me great pleasure and I hope it comes true; then we can talk better in person about our troubles, put them all in a sack, shut them in with cepinetto so that he can amuse himself carrying them, and we will laugh and mock him, for he thought he would get the better of us and instead we got the better of him.5

5. The thought that all these things end very soon and then we have eternal joy makes everything nothing, and with all our love we embrace every suffering, because it alone prepares eternal joy for us.6

Bless me, for I am in haste, as I remain your very poor

Sr. ANNA M. ROSA GATTORNO

She should not be annoyed at having to invite those gentlemen to the examinations. There should also be prizes for the best pupils. She should look after herself, and when the examinations are over she will come to Piacenza. Courage and calm, for it is God's Work. If she had money she would send it.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. I don't know why you took the matter of the boarding fee so hotly, when in reality there was no reproach in it.1 Be cheerful, don't be annoyed about inviting those gentlemen to the examinations; try to work with Squarzoni, and he will tell Don Ignazio and Monsignor and everyone, and Ninetta.2

2. We gave prizes of little value, but they are needed. Tell Bishop Giordani, tell Mgr Mariano, and if they come, it is for them to hand out the prizes.3

3. I am sorry to hear you are ill; for charity's sake take care of yourself, and when you have finished the examinations come here for a while. Don't worry.4

4. It is time you became strong women and nothing less; grow and be strengthened in the spirit of God, the only thing we must want and seek with tireless zeal.5

5. Providence is truly scarce, but when I die you will have everything. Enough; let us leave everything to God.6

6. Try to do well and don't get agitated, but do everything calmly. Courage, for it is God's Work, so we must fight cepinetto.7

7. As for money, I wish I had some to send you, but for now everything is going swimmingly!! Goodbye; the Lord bless you; so on the 14th I will have them pray that everything goes well for you.8

The Lord bless you; believe me always your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

She expresses her gratitude for all he has done for the Institute. She will send him a box of lozenges. She remains anxious about the outcome of the Constitutions.

Your Most Reverend Excellency,

1. My small ability does not allow me to express to Your Most Reverend Excellency in fitting terms my gratitude for all You do and have done for our poor Institute.1 I lay everything at the feet of God Most High, that He in his bounty may reward so great a Benefactor of ours.

2. I receive from the Superior there the pleasant task of getting You another box like the one I brought You before, and I hasten to obtain it.2 My soul is always somewhat agitated by fear about the approval of the Rule; only when Mgr Mariano writes me a word of encouragement do I try to persuade myself that my anxiety comes from the shock I suffered last time, as Your Most Reverend Excellency well knows.3

3. If my health allowed, I would gladly hurry there for the day of the girls' examinations,4 so as to have the good fortune of kissing Your Ring and receiving Your Apostolic blessing, which, prostrate at Your feet, I ask of You, remaining Your Most Reverend Excellency's most humble Sr. A. MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

She tells her about her health. She has received the telegram; there is still time before Saturday, the day of the examinations. If the Lord wants her to come, he will give her health.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. I am writing from bed because Sr. A. Vincenza is in Genoa. For two days I have had a fever, which has made me quite ill. Today it seems somewhat better; don't worry; you know my weakness is such that the least thing is enough to knock me down; it is rheumatic fever. I give you these details so that you will not be anxious.1

2. I see from the telegram that the examinations are on Saturday.2 If the Lord wants me to come, he will give me health and strength; if not, when they are over you will come to me.

3. Tell Mgr Mariano3 that the state of my health is what prevents me from coming. Enough; there are still some days until Saturday, so let us hope.

Goodbye; I am your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

God bless you.

She is in poor health. The addressee should come at once, after giving the instructions mentioned. She should travel with a companion, or alone if that is not possible.1

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. I am writing from bed; my dear, read these lines and then come at once; tell Sr. A. Eletta to treat the Vernengo sisters with every kindness.2

2. Take no further steps; come at once; let there be no more talk of examinations;3 blessed be God.

3. Gather all the sisters; read them this letter without letting them see the handwriting, then keep it yourself. Don't buy the box for Mgr Giordani any more;4 leave everything; come quickly.

4. Greet everyone for me. Goodbye. If you come with Mamma,5 bring no one; otherwise find a companion; otherwise commend yourself to God: God is with you.

I am your affectionate MOTHER ROSA

She gives news of her health. She should send off Sr. A. Giovanna; as soon as the Mother has the strength to travel she will come for the examinations.

A.M.F.

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us

My daughter

Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate

1. Here is my news. I am up; I won't speak of my weakness, for it is extreme; I can say I have never had it [so bad]. Alas, I am growing old and strengthless!

2. Listen, don't worry about Maria's 10 L.1 On Monday send Sr. A. Giovanna alone; instruct her well on what to do, and let her travel by day.2

3. Today I will write to Mgr Mariano, and as soon as my strength allows I will come and the examinations will be held. Be of good heart. Let us hope providence will come.3

4. It would have been better to have Maria clothed [in the habit],4 since she died in the house. Well, it's done now. Cheer up; you should have given her a purge.

Goodbye; I am tired; I am your

Affectionate MOTHER ROSA

She is sorry to hear that he can no longer celebrate Sunday Mass at the Sampierdarena House, as he has for many years. She asks him to find another religious in his place, and hopes he will continue his kind interest in the House.

Most Reverend Don Luigi,

1. I am very sorry to hear that you absolutely cannot go on Sundays to celebrate Holy Mass (as you have so charitably done for so long)1 in that House at Sampierdarena. If this is the Lord's will, and Your Reverence sees it as better to say it in the Parish, patience.

2. It only remains for me to ask you to try to find another Religious who might go in your place. If your occupations do not allow it, kindly write and tell me. I trust that the said house will continue to experience your charity.

3. Awaiting your reply, please accept the esteem and respect of one who is honoured to call herself Your Reverence's most humble Sr. A. MARIA ROSA GATTORNO

to divine justice, deeply felt and widespread in the spirituality of her time, had a strong influence on M. Rosa's "piety".
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc291: Maria Carnevali was ill, as was Delfina Ferrari. For the latter cf. L 206, n. 3.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc293: Sr. A. Maddalena Terzaghi. Cf. L 211, n. 3; 216. Her return home for lack of vocation had already been decided, but the young woman asked forgiveness, resolved to change her life. The Mother trusted her, urged her to pray and to have others pray, and left the final decision about her to Fr Tornatore. Cf. L of 26 April 1872 from Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc294: She refers to problems put before her. The pious busybodies, the false devotees who make holiness consist in devotions and outward rites; ...they put on a show for me, they are useless to me.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc295: These are the essential values of the FSA. Cf. Rule 1869, pp. 19-24, the virtues of charity and simplicity.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc296: Somewhere, i.e. in some place where the Institute has Houses, or elsewhere, for foundations. The Mother House, cradle of the Institute, and the little room, place of her refuge and of intimate converse with her crucified Beloved, exerted on her a nostalgic pull of inexpressible mystical experiences.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc298:
Pester. Keep pressing Town Councillor Giuseppe Grandi to get the Town Council to approve the necessary and urgent works on the council-owned building in Via della Morte, where the Boys' School opened and run by the FSA operated. This involved building the enclosure wall and cutting down the fig trees that blocked light to the ground-floor rooms, moving the boys' latrines into the courtyard, etc.

Cf. L of Parish Priest Elia Magnani to M. Rosa of 4.10.72. AFSA, CbM.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc302: She prays every day in full trust that God will accept her poor prayers and grant her wishes.

Sr. A. Eufemia Mirisola. She was unwell. She died in the house in Via della Morte, Piacenza, on 20 November 1872.

She did well to break off a conversation (it is not known with whom or why), but her attitude, her inner disposition, should have been different.

The word anger wounds her, because it offends the most sweet and gentle heart of the Holy Mother.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc318: Evidently the girl had a contagious disease.

To the postulants: Rosa Bertuzzi (Sr. A. Battistina) and Giacinta Pizzorno (Sr.

...a clothed postulant (that is, a novice) not from Nizza. The clothing took place on 19 May in the Houses of Piacenza, Sampierdarena and Ferrara. Cf.

L 237, n. 1; 233, 4.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc342: She and Sr. A. Ernesta Savani are to leave for Nizza on Monday 20 May, because help is needed, Sr. A. Teresa Guaini being seriously ill.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc343: With the last clothing the Postulancy was left empty, but she can be sure that more will come; she has written to Fr Tornatore to send some.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc344: Cepinetto is having a grand ball because Carlotta is cross and drives everyone to despair; but she works... she has made two caps for two benefactors: Town Councillor Giuseppe Grandi and Secretary Merli. Carlotta adds in her own hand a postscript: my mamma is stingy and cruel, she never gives me [money]; poor Carlotta like a corner (= put in a corner, neglected).
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc345: She had written on the same subject to Fr Agostino Donadio. Cf. L 231.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc346: ...in three hands: in three sittings; ...day of the Holy Spirit, i.e. Pentecost.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc347: While writing to Sr. A. Francesca, she is in spirit addressing the Superiors of the other Communities.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc348: Silence as the atmosphere of the religious House is the environmental precondition for the community's growth in Christ, in mutual charity and goodness, in a harmony of purpose that becomes attunement in being and acting.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc349: Favoured by such a peaceful environment, the FSA lives interior silence, the mysterious reality indwelt by God, where He speaks the ineffable language of sweetness and love.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc350: Having no time to answer the girls' letters, she writes a few words for them, tacitly asking the Superior to read them what concerns them directly.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc351: She forgets to specify the room assigned to Sr. A. Eufemia Mirisole.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc352: ...I remember: I recall at this moment that perhaps you sleep in that room; well, you can move back to your usual room.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc353: It now occurs to her that she would have liked, if the necessary money were available, to have a dividing partition built, to create a single room for the Superior.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc354: Another alteration: to have the door of the little room opening on the large hall closed and a small one opened to the interior, so that the girls no longer pass through the courtyard, or rather by the outside "well staircase", but by the smaller inside stairs. And so they could use the privy close by.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc355: Giulio Sforza Fogliani, owner of the Casa Dal Verme, which on 26 March 1866 he had sold to M. Rosa Gattorno for 40,000 Fr. Cf. L 224, n. 4.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc356:
It has often happened that a visiting Priest meets a girl going down to the cellar; but there is also a danger for the smallest:

the well.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc359: Giuseppe Grandi, Town Councillor, friend and benefactor. His mother, long ill, had probably died. Cf. L 218, n. 6.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc361: The date is deduced from the calendar, since the letter was written on the vigil of Pentecost, 18 May, and also from the context.

Serafina Lorenzi, and her two Novices (the first two listed above) to return to their own community after the ceremony. But while the Superior refused to stay, out of obedience to the Mother, whose letter she showed, and indeed left with Sr. A. Geltrude, the Superior of the house and Don Luigi kept back Sr. Eletta, taking her on some pretext into a room so that she would not notice the departure of Superior Serafina.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc364: She would have been displeased not only by the disobedience but also because there were two Sisters ill in the Genoa House. Cf. L of Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi to M. Rosa of 19.5.72. AFSA, DI, 3.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc365:
This was the religious name of Adelaide Vernengo, sister of Sr. A.

Concetta.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc366: For the moment she does not speak to her of the life annuity, having entrusted it to Don Antonio Accinelli. Cf. L 177, n. 7.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc367: She should ask Don Luigi Decavi whether the Daughters of Saint Anne will be called to the new hospital at Sampierdarena or not. Cf. L 239.

Before writing to Parish Priest Magnani the Foundress had sought advice.

Town Clerk Merli sent a letter on the subject on 30 May 1872 to the Secretary General, Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: "The Mother is the sole and absolute owner and director of the School". AFSA, Mother House.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc369: The same letter also says: (in such capacity) for the coming national holiday she will receive from the Council for the said School the sum of L. 200.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc372: She had gone to Piacenza for a few days.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc373: the favour, i.e. the letter of commendation she had asked him for. Cf. L 235.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc375: She had seen to the girls' sea-bathing in good time (cf. L 211, n. 9) and continued to follow it up.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc376: He served as administrator of various charitable foundations and also devoted himself to works of zeal.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc377: The Sisters were truly poor, "entrusted to providence". The Superior, Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi, or another Sister in her place, went almost every day "begging" and obtained meagre alms, barely enough for the daily needs of the community, which besides the Sisters included two or three needy girls.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc378: ...poor new house: it had been born poor on 17 April 1871 for the free nursing and care of the sick in their homes, and lived poorly, with no income but the alms "begged" from prominent citizens.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc380: ...in accordance with their wishes. By the plural she clearly means to include the Pastor of the Diocese, Mgr Salvatore Magnasco, whose Secretary the addressee was. With skill and prudence M. Rosa reveals her secret wish to obtain from Mgr Magnasco the letter of "commendation" to the Holy See, which he is reluctant to grant. In a way, even "a line" from his secretary has evidential value.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc381: This is Don Angelo Ricchini. Cf. Letters 1, p. 529.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc382: Cf. L 220, 2. She had handed the Constitutions to Card. Vannicell April 72.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc384: acting rightly: acting well in handling these tempora afflict my soul.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc387:
One thing alone: the only support in her extreme existential poverty and her trials and sufferings: God and his fatherly dispositions. He draws her inwardly;

being within his life gives her the vital energy of being and acting, to spend and consume herself until death solely for Jesus. Immersed in God's pacifying strength, all agitation subsides and earthly reality takes on the outline of transience.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc388: That is, of the Rule, which is still being revised (cf. L 244, 1).
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc389: As in Piacenza and Sampierdarena, the "girls in danger" are offered "that intellectual, moral and religious culture which serves to form persons useful to society, perfect and holy Christians". Rule 1869, Chap. 14, 1. And as in the other houses, the sisters devote themselves to nursing the sick at home.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc390:
Want, extreme poverty, is a cause of suffering but also of growth in trust in the Father; but she feels sharper pain from wounds of another kind:

misunderstandings, criticism, obstacles, deaths... These are the fabric of daily acceptance, in faith and love, of God's will.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc392: Enjoy: friendly words to friends present in God and sharing his fullness of joy.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc393: Fr Antonio Angelini SJ. Cf. L 231, n. 4.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc394: The date is inferred from the context.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc395: At Novi Ligure station she had met Alessandro's teacher and received good news from him about his health, conduct and studies.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc396: Don Accinelli is at the house of Signora Paola Airenta in Sampierdarena, engaged in constant attendance on her son Girolamo, in a desperate condition after an attempted suicide.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc397: Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi. She worried about the Mother's health when she did not receive letters in her own hand.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc398: This is the immediate, brief reply to the addressee's letter written the same day, 4 June, as soon as she reached Genoa. The Mother had sent her to Genoa to deal with the Ricchini case. Cf. L 244, 1-2.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc399: Sr. A. Eletta Bruschi. Sr. A. Vincenza had written to her that it was severe diarrhoea, so she suggests forbidding her fruit.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc400: The subject of her message to her mother is unknown. In a later letter (9.6.72) Sr. A. Vincenza writes that she had said to her mother what she had been told; she also says she had received from her father, without asking, a note "on the sale" (she gives no further details).
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc401: Simplicity, trust, familiarity, spontaneity, openness of heart in intimate dealings: human virtues that mark the character of Rosa Gattorno, as humble as she was great and dear in the eyes of men and to the heart of God.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc402: To Sr. Paola Bucciotti. She was to keep and use for the needs of the house the payment from the Vernengo annuity (cf. L 177, n. 7) and also write to the father-in-law of Sr. A. Benvenuta Grino, who had received the religious habit on 19 May. Note that the Rule allowed widows to be accepted.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc403: This is a Genoese saying whose meaning we do not know.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc405: If my head never... in her brisk, effective style she expresses her strong desire for effective help to free her from the persistent headache and the worry of the lawsuit with Don Angelo Ricchini.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc406: Superior Francesca had written that she had received no news from her.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc407: She had had cleaning and repair work done. She approves what she had agreed in both cases.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc409: Sr. A. Vincenza, returning from Genoa, was to accompany Sr. A. Panasia Bellardi, who was to go to Ferrara, but not with Sr. A. Giovannina, as she had been told.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc410: ...Paoletta's son. Cf. L 246, n. 3. Signora Airenta did indeed, as Sr. A. Vincenza wrote to Sr. A. Francesca, fall seriously ill (cf. L 17.6.1872). The news of the young man's death given by Sr. A. Paola to Mother Rosa was however inaccurate: he was still alive.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc411: The letter of Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni, Superior of the Ferrara House, is dated 3 June 1872. Maria Massari, a boarder, protégée of Count Francesco Caracciolo. On the sea-bathing cf. L 211, n. 9; 241, 1.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc412: Sr. A. Francesca had complained of the girls, so undisciplined that she had had to punish them. Sr. A. Angelica Dematteis also caused her suffering with her public complaints at having been transferred from Ferrara to Piacenza.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc413: She commends her to the Father, placing her in his benevolence, in peace and serenity; she supports her with her prayer that she may speak wisely to judges and lawyers, and asks the Lord for strength and courage so that she may bear the burdens of the heavy task in union with his will and bring it to a good end.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc416: In the unfortunate event of losing the case and so having to pay Ricchini the sum he claimed, what to do? She suggests asking the lawyers' opinion on whether the Vernengo Sisters should secure their "life annuity" by a mortgage on the Palazzo Dal Verme. And she ends by telling her to have the notarial deed drawn up. For the Vernengos cf. L 177, n. 7; for the Ricchini case Letters 1, p. 529.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc417: Sr. A. Panasia Bellardi was being transferred from Nizza to Ferrara.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc418: On the way to Ferrara she was to stop in Bologna to visit Countess Maria Anna Trotti.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc419: God bless you. For this daughter on her own, engaged in difficult and important temporal affairs, she asks and wishes a blessing: abundant participation in the divine life and a deep experience of the all that He is and the nothing that she is. For pity's sake, beware of vainglory! Let her not grow vain, thinking herself good for something!
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc421: She wanted to entrust the Ricchini case to Sr. A. Vincenza's uncle, the lawyer Domenico Boccardo, dispensing with the lawyer De Bernardi.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc422: She will warn Fr Tornatore, who was also involved in the case, to refrain from writing about it.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc423: She repeats the reason to give for changing lawyers.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc425: Your uncle: the lawyer Boccardo; that Priest: Don Angelo Ricchini.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc426: Because of her intestinal illness, fruit was harmful to her.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc427: Since November 1871 the Community had lived on the 2nd floor of a building at Via S. Maria di Castello 8. It was advisable to find a more suitable dwelling, independent of other tenants.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc429: Sr. A. Santina Solenghi, who was in the Genoa house. For the report of Sr. A. Vincenza cf. her letter of 11 June 1872.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc431: Don Luigi's indolence. He had not wanted to go to Genoa to speak to the lawyer De Bernardi because of the rain.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc432: She refers to the son of Signora Paola Airenta, who had attempted suicide. Cf. L 248, 6.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc434: Sr. A. Vincenza had been favourably impressed by the running of the house.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc435: Maria, Princess D'Annenkoff. Cf. L 14, n. 6; 44, n. 9. Sr. A. Vincenza replied on the 9th that she had returned, but she had not seen her.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc436: Maria Maddalena of the Dukes Durazzo had entered the Institute as a postulant but had then gone home. Cf. L 161; 163; 164; 169; 264, n. 2.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc437: Advice for Superior Serafina Lorenzi. First tell her to set about finding a larger house and explain the legal requirements for opening a school. They must not get into a mess! If the desks she has obtained are not needed, she can give them to the Sampierdarena House. You could hint at it... fit: a significant pedagogical touch: respect for persons, attention and regard for the character and role of each.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc438: Her heart full of God's consolation at her daughter's good conduct, she is glad to express the fullness of motherly feeling. Praise is necessary to spur greater generosity, just as firm methods are necessary when needed. She faithfully keeps to this wise teaching principle and recalls it to those responsible for formation.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc439: Sr. A. Vincenza had written to her on 5 June '72. Cf. L 251, n. 5. God is there. The house is God's and not merely the community's dwelling. The signs that prove this are clear evidence of it: silence, good little girls (diligent, obedient, sensible), work.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc440: Sr. A. Vincenza had also written: "They have a workroom with so much work it is a pleasure to see, so many bolts of linen for shirts, and the Superior told me that every evening they bring her 30 shirts made by the girls". Mother Rosa's comment is apt: if time is wholly given to God in keeping the law of work, common to all mankind, there is surely peace.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc441:
To give a present... provide a suitable dress for going to the seaside.

Touches of exquisitely motherly delicacy. Daily earnings were barely enough for food, but the new dress is the Mother's gift and brings joy to the dear little ones. There is Providence: does not the heavenly Father clothe even the lilies of the field?
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc442: She should also provide clothing for the Sisters, with due economy, of course.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc443: The well-known life annuity. Cf. L 177, n. 7.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc445: Go to Archbishop Salvatore Magnasco; ...his secretary, the priest Giovanni Battista Sacco. The Superior of the Genoa house, Sr. A. Serafina Lorenzi, had gone there at the end of May 1872. Cf. L 243.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc446: Don Luigi Decavi, Sr. A. Concetta and Sr. A. Giuseppa Vernengo...; the dear little girls. She trusted in their prayer for the many graces she awaited.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc447:
Her crosses were concrete, heavy and many: the debts, the Ricchini lawsuit, illnesses and problems of the ever more numerous Sisters, the matter of the Constitutions, which she saw stranded, and the many others springing up every day. Sr. A.

Paola — the Mother had learned it secretly — also had a private sorrow: she had recently learned of the removal from the Institute of Fr Tornatore, to whom she was filially attached. Cf. L 214, 3. ...Let us hold fast to the tree of the cross. It is the only way to cross the stormy sea of life.

" Courage is the active aspect of fortitude, that special firmness of spirit which is not shaken by evils and dangers; resignation is endurance in bearing difficult things. Both are needed to undertake arduous things and overcome adversities in carrying forward the Lord's Work.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc448: Courage is the active side of fortitude, that firmness of spirit which is not shaken by evils and dangers; resignation is endurance in bearing hard things. Both are needed to undertake arduous tasks and overcome adversity in carrying forward the Lord's Work.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc449: In these very personal expressions one hears the echo of Mary's Magnificat.

A group of the older girls had for some time agreed together and made a novena to Our Lady for Superior Francesca to be transferred. notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc451: She also threatens Corina Canepari with expulsion. She had entered in May 1868 with two sisters and was 16.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc452: The Sister transferred from Ferrara. Cf. L 248, n. 7.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc454: Giuseppe Grandi, as benefactor and Town Councillor, could have the works mentioned here included in those belonging to the Council.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc455: Sr. A. Francesca had consulted the House doctor, Sante Albertazzi, who, having heard the Mother's symptoms, had prescribed them.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc456: Sr. A. Fortunata Zucconi was not improving despite medical treatment.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc458: Two uniform dresses of the former postulant Antonietta Merigi and the other of Maddalena Carmeli... for Piacenza they will be fine, since the Mother House was reserved for boarders only, whereas in Ferrara there was the School attended by both boarders and day pupils.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc459: The Parish Priest of Nizza Monferrato, Ludovico Bisio. The Mother wanted him to go to the Alberoni College at S. Lazzaro so that he could confer with Fr Tornatore.

"We must look to being together for an eternity".

The blessing of the Eternal Father be with us My blessed daughter Blessed be our Mother Saint Anne, Mother of the Immaculate 1. Today I received your letter with a sample of cotton cloth. To tell you the truth I don't like it at all; rather, if you can't find any, I will get it here from our merchant and send you two bolts on Monday, addressed to Don Luigi; I hope to have the cheese too.1 My dear, you know well that getting anything takes more than one can imagine.

2. In Genoa there are two sisters for whom the doctor has prescribed sea-bathing, and since they are so near the sea at S. P. D'Arena, they had better take it there. So they will come to you for 15 days and then, when the treatment is over, return to Genoa.

3. You ask how to arrange the bathing. I leave you to do as you think best, also for the sisters; one who badly needs it is the cook; the others, whomever you think.

an invitation to trustful abandonment to God, moment by moment.

She proposes as a model St Rose of Lima, the humble, simple virgin, wholly given over to love in an attitude of obedience, in sincere stripping of poverty.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc561:
"...a sure method" to apply and follow in governing the community.

The instruction on "discernment" has several stages.

First: attentive and kindly listening to the sister's advice and proposals, without however taking any decision. The Superior reserves to herself reflection and decision.

Second: the Superior reflects carefully on what has been suggested, asks God's counsel, seeking objective truth in prayer. Third: carrying out, with order and firmness, whatever of the suggestions she has judged "good and sensible", disregarding the inappropriate ones.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc562: Foreseeing, as an expert judge of people and things, the case of the sister persisting in the role of "adviser", she gives suitable instructions. And she concludes with a "golden maxim" suitable not only for Adelaide, of a rather lively and sensitive character, but for all who hold responsibility for government.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc563: If she were still not convinced, she must go deeper, enlightening her and helping her discover the underlying motive of her conduct. In any case, she can turn to the Mother.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc564: These are reflections springing from her heart as mother and formator, aimed at cutting evil at the root: self-love.

notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc70002:
As for that person... it is all down to rigidity and his exalted doctrine, but more to the rigidity he showed me. In a few words she expresses a reality as painful as it was incomprehensible to her: the charges against the Rule are turned against its author. The following points were in fact made:

a. It is too rigid.

b. Making Saint Anne speak is absurd; making her say things not known from the holy books arouses some suspicion of heresy.

c. Fr Tornatore is not suited to guide the Institute; "He may be a Saint, but not good for this". AFSA, 72, RdP.
notes.lettere-en-v2-fnc70003: In practice, the Institute is saved only by her presence. Otherwise they would have dissolved it. But these do not seem good reasons to her, because she feels incapable and ignorant (less than a donkey). Convinced of her utter nothingness, and in need of counsel, she turns to Saint Anne.
